All round it storms of trouble blow, And waves of sorrow roll; Cold winds and winter storms beat through, And pain the tenant-soul. Alas, how frail our state!" said I, And thus went mourning on, Till sudden from the cleaving-sky A gleam of glory shone. My soul felt all the glory come, air; And breathed her native Then she remembered heaven her home, And she a prisoner here. Straight she began to change her key, And joyful in her pains, She sang the frailty of her clay In pleasurable strains.
